RESULT: DONE
CHANGED: src/mem_mcp/mindmap/workflow_crud.py, tests/unit/mindmap/test_workflow_crud.py
TESTS: alembic upgrade head -> no errors (the test DB lacked the workflow tables until then); pytest tests/unit/mindmap/test_workflow_crud.py -q -> 11 passed in 1.71s; ruff check on both files -> All checks passed!; mypy -> Success: no issues found in 345 source files; python tools/lint_tenant_scope.py -> OK: no tenant-scope violations across 185 files. I did not run the full `pytest -q`.
NOTES:
- Inputs are `StageSpec` and `TransitionSpec` dataclasses defined in workflow_crud.py. Transitions refer to stages by name, and ordinals follow list order.
- `materialise_legacy_workflow` uses `tenant_id` as `created_by`, since the signature has no actor.
- `remap_workflow_stages` maps onto the team's active workflow. It raises `WorkflowNotFoundError` if there is none and `StageNotFoundError` if a target name isn't in that workflow. It also sets `work_items.workflow_id` to the active workflow on the rows it moves. The plan didn't say whether to set `workflow_id`; I set it because `current_stage` is only authoritative when `workflow_id` is set.
- The permission check uses `created_by` in create and `actor_tenant_id` in activate and remap. `get_workflow` raises `WorkflowNotFoundError` if no workflow is active.
- A duplicate workflow name raises a generic `WorkflowError`, since no more specific error exists in `workflow_errors.py`.
